summary: A declaration-level design of finite and infinite root stacks and Yun–Zhang’s ramified geometric class field theory. It owns the reserved root-stack definition, imports the parent’s arithmetic reciprocity and existing geometric suppliers, and records exact stack-sheaf and typed-prototype gaps. All 28 items of the first route are assigned; the independent 38-item symplectic-central-value route is preserved in a split proposal rather than silently absorbed or discarded. The affine invariant-ring step is factored through the native μ_n Hopf coaction, its axioms, root weights and point comparison; geometric carriers remain open. Six native root-trivialization comparison nodes now expose the computed unit coefficient and root-arrow scalar equations; no geometric carrier or generic section tensor operation is duplicated. Continuation supplies fpqc descent and thirteen finite/infinite root-transition/Kummer proof leaves; it corrects the inherited infinite H1 topology and separates ordinary stacks, algebraic properties and coarse suppliers. Canonical integration adds the actual finite affine action comparison, weighted tensor coordinates, explicit kernel/module-cokernel maps, sharp injectivity/surjectivity criteria and unit inverse; the branch and normalized-coframe torsors remain distinct.

nodes.statement: For n≥1 and a line bundle with section (L,s) on a scheme X or an algebraic stack X, define √[n]{(L,s)/X} on T→X as the groupoid of root objects of (L_T,s_T). Pullback and its coherent isomorphisms define the fibred stack. For an effective Cartier divisor D use (O_X(D),s_D). Arbitrary exponents use the fppf topology; the étale description is asserted only when n is invertible.
hypotheses: The exponent n is a positive integer; the scheme or stack base and all base changes use the stated fppf topology.
proofSteps: Use the supplier’s line-bundle pullback and descent, retaining the root isomorphism and section equation.
Root-object morphisms descend since equality of sheaf maps is local; glue the line bundles, sections and φ effectively.
For a stack base, pull back to an atlas and descend with the same definition; do not replace the stack base by a coarse space.
acceptance: At n=1 the projection is an equivalence. For an invertible section it is an equivalence for every n, including p|n.

nodes.title: Root stacks as a two-fibre product
nodes.statement: Let A=[A¹/G_m] classify a line bundle with section and [n]:A→A take its n-th tensor power. The root stack is X×_{A,[n]}A with its universal root. For a stack base this is a two-fibre product, including the specified isomorphism, not an equality pullback of coarse points.

proofSteps: Unpack a two-pullback object: (x,(M,t),φ) with φ identifying (Mⁿ,tⁿ) and (L_x,s_x).
Identify arrows with the root-object compatibility equations.
Use the supplier’s two-Yoneda recognition of fibred-category equivalence.
acceptance: The isomorphism φ is retained, even when all geometric coarse points agree.

nodes.title: Affine quotient presentation
nodes.statement: If X=Spec A and (L,s) is trivialized with s=f, then √[n]{(L,s)/X}≃[Spec AdjoinRoot(Tⁿ−f)/μ_n], with the diagonalizable action already constructed. This is a quotient stack with torsors, not an orbit set.
hypotheses: The exponent n is a positive integer; the scheme or stack base and all base changes use the stated fppf topology.
proofSteps: Use root-trivialization-equation and root-arrow-scalars on native trivializations: objects have unit u with u zⁿ=f and arrows have z_b=w z_a, u_b wⁿ=u_a. The generic quotient-stack/torsor construction remains SF.1; these scalar equations are its actual root-specific input.

Use the affine coaction and its laws. In trivial coordinates φ(eⁿ)=u with u a unit and section b e satisfying u bⁿ=f. Compatible normalized coframes e↦a form Spec A[a]/(aⁿ−u), which is the unit-parameter torsor by affine-torsor-unit-inverse and the imported finite-free/torsor criterion. The equivariant root-chart coordinate is x↦ab. It scales with weight one. Do not treat Spec A[x]/(xⁿ−f) as a torsor over Spec A at the branch locus.
On the torsor the root section is a function t satisfying tⁿ=f.
Conversely descend the trivial root line and function on an equivariant torsor; show the two operations inverse on objects and arrows.
acceptance: When f=0 the chart is Spec A[t]/tⁿ; its nilpotents remain present.

For s(x)=0 pass to the reduction t=0, then identify the residual classifying gerbe.
For s(x)≠0 the solution scheme is a μ_n-torsor and its quotient stack is the point.

nodes.title: Coarse-space projection
nodes.statement: For a scheme base X, the projection of the root stack to X is its coarse-space morphism. For an algebraic-stack base, it is relative coarse over X: after scheme base change it has the preceding coarse property. It is not an assertion that X is an absolute algebraic space.
hypotheses: The exponent n is a positive integer; the scheme or stack base and all base changes use the stated fppf topology.
proofSteps: Apply the affine-invariants theorem to the actual Hopf coaction, in arbitrary characteristic. The native monic basis also gives faithful coefficient inclusion in the nontrivial case.
Apply the supplier’s diagonalizable quotient coarse-space theorem, with its universal property; glue across trivializations.
Use base change to interpret the stack-base statement relatively.
acceptance: At n=1 over BG the projection is identity BG; the absolute coarse space remains the coarse space of BG.

nodes.title: Regularity and the tame DM condition
nodes.statement: If X is regular and D is a regular effective Cartier divisor, √[n]{(O(D),s_D)/X} is regular; when n is invertible on X it is Deligne–Mumford with μ_n inertia over D and trivial inertia outside D. If a geometric branch point has characteristic dividing n, its μ_n inertia is not étale, so the stack is not DM there. An empty divisor still gives X in every characteristic.
hypotheses: The exponent n is a positive integer; the scheme or stack base and all base changes use the stated fppf topology.
proofSteps: Locally choose a regular parameter f cutting out D; the equation tⁿ=f replaces that parameter and gives a regular chart.
For invertible n the finite diagonalizable stabilizer is étale; descend regularity through the atlas.
At an actual branch point use the computed μ_n inertia and its nonreduced characteristic-dividing part to obstruct the DM diagonal.
acceptance: On a DVR the n=2 root is regular in odd residue characteristic; the assertion is not that arbitrary sections cut regular divisors.

nodes.title: Infinite root stacks
nodes.statement: Define √[infinity]{(L,s)/X} as the two-inverse limit of the finite root stacks indexed by positive integers ordered by divisibility, on the fpqc scheme site. Its objects over T are compatible finite root objects with transition isomorphisms satisfying cocycles; arrows are compatible systems of root isomorphisms. It is an fpqc stack, hence also an fppf stack by restriction, and is not asserted to be an algebraic stack of finite presentation. Its affine quotient uses fpqc torsors.
hypotheses: All finite exponents are positive. Infinite root objects and quotient torsors use the fpqc scheme site.
proofSteps: Use the already planned compatible-family carrier, retaining objects, arrows and unit/composition equations.
Every finite root is an fpqc stack by root-fpqc-descent. Apply the imported limit-stack-descent theorem to those components and their finite transitions.

For a single effective Cartier divisor, TV17 Proposition3.5 identifies the compatible system with its logarithmic infinite root. The local quotient comparison is its separate infinite-affine-quotient leaf.
acceptance: A set-theoretic inverse limit of isomorphism classes discards coherent automorphism data and is insufficient.

nodes.title: The infinite reduced DVR fibre
nodes.statement: The reduced closed fibre of the infinite root of a DVR with residue field k is the inverse system of the root gerbes of the normal line, banded by lim_n μ_n=Ẑ(1). It is noncanonically equivalent to B_kẐ(1); a chosen trivialization of the normal line gives a compatible neutralization. The neutralization is not part of the canonical root stack.
hypotheses: Finite roots are defined fppf and satisfy the stronger fpqc descent theorem. Infinite systems and infinite torsors use fpqc descent.
proofSteps: Use the normal line to identify each reduced finite closed fibre with its n-th-root gerbe.
A trivialization of that one-dimensional k-space supplies compatible trivial root objects at all n.
The automorphisms form lim μ_n, and coherent descent gives the banded gerbe; use the source’s reduced-fibre convention for the infinite limit.
acceptance: The full fibre retains nilpotent finite charts; only the reduced gerbe is identified with the classifying gerbe.

nodes.title: Kummer classes of infinite-gerbe points
nodes.statement: After choosing a neutralization of the infinite reduced DVR gerbe over k, its k-points up to isomorphism identify with H1_fpqc(k,G), where G=lim_n μ_n, and with lim_n H1_fppf(k,μ_n)=lim_n k×/(k×)^n. Infinite torsors are fpqc; the finite Kummer calculation is fppf. The full groupoid retains G(k) automorphisms, and changing the neutralization changes the chosen origin.
hypotheses: A DVR with residue field k of arbitrary characteristic and a chosen compatible neutralization.
G is the fpqc inverse-limit sheaf of all μ_n, with power transition maps.
proofSteps: The neutralization identifies the reduced gerbe with fpqc G-torsors.
The Kummer torsor-limit comparison gives its actual finite tower, including the quotient identifications.
Apply kummer-limit-iso-detection for injectivity on classes and kummer-limit-class-lift for surjectivity; do not commute isomorphism classes with limits without these leaves.
Apply the exact finite fppf Kummer comparison at each exponent and retain its transition maps. The result is an identification with a chosen origin, not a loss of the automorphism groupoid.
acceptance: Changing neutralization translates the Kummer classes; no canonical origin is asserted.
The compatible roots-of2 torsor overQ is retained despite having no fppf local trivialization; H1_fppf(k,G) is not substituted for H1_fpqc(k,G).

nodes.title: The graded root Picard stack

proofSteps: Import the ordinary line-bundle Picard stack and restriction to R.
Take the root-gerbe two-pullback for the restricted line bundle; do not require a section.
Tensor and dual root data with the imported coherent line-bundle isomorphisms.
acceptance: Pic^d is a torsor component, with no chosen degree-one point required.

nodes.title: Square-action presentation of the root Picard stack
nodes.statement: Let Pic_{X,R} classify (L,γ:L|_R≅O_R). Then Pic_X^√R≃[Pic_{X,R}/[2]Res_{R/k}G_m], where the acting group changes the rigidification through its square. The forgetful morphism to Pic_X is a Res_{R/k}μ₂-gerbe.

proofSteps: Trivialize K_R fppf-locally; ι supplies the rigidification γ.
Changing the root-line frame by u changes γ by u², giving the square-action quotient.
The kernel is Res μ₂; verify the relative automorphism group and local lift property.
acceptance: The unsquared action gives ordinary Pic_X and loses the ramification gerbe.

nodes.title: Étale-local surjectivity of the root norm on units
nodes.statement: Nm^√R:ν_*G_m,X′→G_m,X^√R is surjective as an étale sheaf under the odd-characteristic double-cover hypotheses.
hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.
proofSteps: Away from R split the double cover étale-locally; the product norm is surjective.
At a branch stalk, for (u,v) with ū=v² choose an étale-local square root a of u with a|_R=v, possible since two and v are units.
The scalar upstairs unit a has norm a²=u and residue v.
acceptance: This is local surjectivity of sheaves, not surjectivity on every ring’s global units.

nodes.title: Local Hilbert 90 with root normalization
nodes.statement: As étale sheaves, ker Nm^√R is the image of u↦u/(σu), and ker(1−σ)=G_m,X inside ν_*G_m,X′. At ramification a root-normalized norm-one u has residue one, so w=1+u is locally a unit and u=w/(σw).
hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.
proofSteps: On the split locus use the explicit norm-one pair (u,u⁻¹).
At a branch point use σu=u⁻¹ and u|_{R′}=1; then 1+u is invertible because two is.
Invariant units descend through the finite-flat cover, giving the left kernel.
acceptance: Ordinary norm-one residue −1 is excluded by the root normalization; 1+u would fail there.

nodes.title: The quadratic root-curve local system
nodes.statement: For the geometrically connected double cover, ν_*Q̄ℓ decomposes into the ± eigensheaves of σ; its anti-invariant restriction to U is rank one, geometrically nontrivial and has inertia −1 exactly at R. Extend it to the root curve through the tame correspondence. The parent’s arithmetic reciprocity gives η_{F′/F}:F×\A_F×→{±1}, which is trivial on the image of O_{√R}×.
hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.
proofSteps: Use the idempotents (1±σ)/2 on rational coefficients, including ℓ=2.
Connectedness of X′ over kbar makes the quadratic geometric character nontrivial; the local branch calculation gives inertia sign.
Local reciprocity identifies the ramified unit character with the residue square character, which vanishes on modified root units.

nodes.statement: The Frobenius trace of L^Pic is a multiplicative Q̄ℓ×-valued function on isomorphism classes of Pic_X^√R(k), normalized to one at the tensor unit. Via the adelic equivalence it defines an idele character. For general input L its range is not restricted to {±1}.

proofSteps: Apply Frobenius to the multiplication isomorphism and take the trace of the rank-one tensor line.
Use the canonical unit to fix the value at e.
Transport through the groupoid equivalence, preserving descent invariance.

nodes.title: Affine root-chart coaction
nodes.statement: Put B=A[t]/(tⁿ−f), using native AdjoinRoot, and H=A[Multiplicative(ZMod n)], using the native Hopf group algebra. Write e_i for its character basis element indexed by i modulo n. Define the unique A-algebra map δ:B→H⊗_A B with δ(t)=e_1⊗t. Constants map to 1⊗a. This is a universal coordinate map, not an action of the geometric-point set.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring, f∈A and n≥1. No reducedness, nonzerodivisor or invertibility-of-n hypothesis is imposed.
proofSteps: In the native group algebra e_1ⁿ=e_0=1 because the character index is modulo n. Hence (e_1⊗t)ⁿ=1⊗f and the quotient polynomial evaluates to zero.
Apply the native AdjoinRoot algebra lift with this root and the coefficient map to H⊗_A B. The algebra-map law fixes constants.
Native quotient algebra-hom extensionality proves uniqueness. Counit and coassociativity are proved in separate nodes, not assumed fields.
acceptance: The map exists for f=0, nonreduced bases and the zero ring.

nodes.title: Invariants of an affine root chart
nodes.statement: For every b∈B=A[t]/(tⁿ−f), δ(b)=1⊗b if and only if b=algebraMap(a) for some a∈A. Thus the scheme-theoretic invariant subalgebra is precisely the coefficient image, for all commutative A, f∈A and n≥1, including characteristic dividing n.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring, f∈A and n≥1. No reducedness, nonzerodivisor or invertibility-of-n hypothesis is imposed.
proofSteps: Separate the subsingleton coefficient-ring case: its unital algebra B and tensor algebra are subsingleton, so both assertions hold with a=0. This avoids invoking the polynomial degree theorem without its nontriviality hypothesis.

For nontrivial A, Xⁿ−f is monic and has nat-degree n. Import the native monic AdjoinRoot power basis and reindex along that equality to write b uniquely as ∑_{0≤i<n} a_i t^i. The generic quotient basis is already library mathematics.

Use the weight lemma and the tensor-product basis of the native group-algebra basis and root power basis. In δ(b), a_i occurs at (i mod n,i); in 1⊗b it occurs at (0,i). For 0<i<n these index pairs differ, forcing a_i=0. This remains valid with torsion or nilpotents; it never divides by n or averages over field-valued points.
Only a_0 remains, giving b=algebraMap(a_0). Conversely the A-algebra-map law and tensor scalar relation give δ(algebraMap(a))=1⊗algebraMap(a).
acceptance: At n=1 every element is a coefficient. At f=0 the nilpotent root powers remain independent. In characteristic p, field-point invariance is strictly weaker than δ-invariance.

nodes.statement: For an actual n-th root object a=(M,t,φ) of (L,s), n≥1, and specified trivializations e:M≅O and l:L≅O, form α=c_n⁻¹ followed by (e⁻¹)ⁿ, φ and l, an automorphism of O. nodes.statement: For 0≤i,j<n, Θ(x^i⊗x^j)=f^⌊(i+j)/n⌋(e_i⊗x^((i+j) mod n)). The exponent is zero or one. The target index σ(i,j)=(i,(i+j) mod n) is a permutation: its inverse sends (i,k) to (i,k−i) when k≥i and to (i,n+k−i) when k<i.

contract.name: The square classes L(X, ρ) and L^*(X, ρ)
contract.statement: L(X, ρ) is the image of L(X, ρ, 1/√q) in ℓ^×/2 when nonzero; in general L^*(X, ρ) = spinor norm(F̄) = (h!·det⟨v_i, v_j⟩)^{−1}(d^h/dt^h)L(X, ρ, t)|_{t=1/√q} ∈ ℓ^×/2, where h (even) is the order of vanishing, the dimension of the generalized fixed space of F on H^1(X_{k̄}, ρ), with basis v_1, …, v_h. For GSp-valued ρ^{(g)} with cyclotomic multiplier and ρ = ρ^{(g)}(−1/2), L(X, ρ^{(g)}) is the square class of L(X, ρ^{(g)}, 1) = L(X, ρ, 1/√q).
contract.note: The second equality is Zassenhaus's formula (Appendix B.9.1) applied to the even-dimensional H^1 of square discriminant.

contract.name: Lemma 3.5.1 and §3.5: square discriminant of H^1
contract.statement: For a closed oriented surface Σ and ρ : π_1(Σ) → Sp_{2r}(ℓ), ℓ finite, the quadratic form on H^*(Σ, ρ) (the cup-product form on H^1, and the Poincaré pairing between H^0 and H^2) has square discriminant. Consequently, by lifting to the Witt vectors and to C, H^1(X_{k̄}, ρ) has square discriminant and L(X, ρ) does not depend on the choice of √q.
contract.note: Proof: the discriminant is a bordism invariant (a Lagrangian image and dim H^* ≡ 0 mod 4), giving MSO_2(BSp_{2r}(ℓ)) = H_2(Sp_{2r}(ℓ), Z) → ℓ^×/2, which vanishes because H_2 has odd order (sourceIssues E3).

contract.name: The trace map and c_et(X, ρ)
contract.statement: For A finite of order prime to p, the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence and the trace H^2(X_{k̄}, A(1)) ≅ A give trace_X : H^3_et(X, A(1)) ≅ H^1(Gal(k̄/k), A) ≅ A (via the Frobenius generator). For ρ : π_1(X) → Sp(ℓ), c_et(X, ρ) := trace_X(ρ^*c_et) ∈ ℓ^×/2 (A = ℓ^×/2 ≅ Z/2).

contract.name: Admissible and GSp-admissible pairs
contract.statement: (X, ρ), with X a smooth projective geometrically irreducible curve over k = F_q and ρ : π_1(X) → Sp_{2r}(ℓ), is admissible if (a1) ρ is geometrically surjective, (a2) q is prime to #Sp_{2r}(ℓ), (a3) q is a square in the prime field of ℓ. It is GSp-admissible (ρ : π_1(X) → GSp_{2r}(ℓ) with cyclotomic multiplier) if (a1)′ the geometric image contains Sp_{2r}(ℓ) and (a2)′ q is prime to #GSp_{2r}(ℓ). Admissible implies GSp-admissible for ρ^{(g)}.

contract.name: Theorem 3.1: the main theorem
contract.statement: Let (X, ρ) be admissible, #ℓ ≡ ±1 (mod 8) and q ≡ 1 (mod 8). Then L(X, ρ) = c_et(X, ρ) in ℓ^×/2 (with L = L^* when the central value vanishes).
contract.note: The proof in v1 does not cover r = 1, #ℓ = 9 (sourceIssues E4).

contract.name: Equivalence of the Sp and GSp formulations
contract.statement: For ρ = ρ^{(g)}(−1/2): L(X, ρ^{(g)}) = L(X, ρ) and c_et(X, ρ^{(g)}) = c_et(X, ρ), since the class on GSp(ℓ) pulls back along π_1(X) → Sp(ℓ) × Ẑ → GSp(ℓ) to c_et ⊗ 1 plus a term in H^2(Sp(ℓ), ℓ^×/2) ⊗ ℓ^×/2 = 0.

contract.name: Lemma 3.9.1: even valuation of central values of compatible systems
contract.statement: Let {σ_λ : π_1(X) → GSp_{2r}(o_{E,λ})} be a compatible system (traces of Frobenius powers in E, independent of λ ∤ p), with L(X, σ, t) ∈ E(t). If λ ∤ 2p and σ_λ has geometric image Zariski dense in Sp_{2r}, then the valuation at λ of L(X, σ) = L(X, σ, 1), if nonzero, is even.
contract.note: The spinor norm of an orthogonal map preserving a unimodular lattice has even valuation (O'Meara 92:5).

contract.name: Larsen's big-image theorem for compatible systems
contract.statement: For a compatible system {σ_λ} with Zariski-dense image, for a density-one set of λ the image of σ_λ in PSp_{2r}(E_λ) contains a conjugate of the image of Sp_{2r}(o_λ) (Larsen, Thm. 3.17).

contract.name: §3.10 (*): Theorem 3.1 determines L-values of compatible systems
contract.statement: Let {σ_λ} be a compatible system of GSp_{2r}-valued representations over X/F_q, q ≡ 1 (mod 8), with L(X, σ) ≠ 0, such that (a) the p-cyclotomic extension of E(√2) has degree > 4r² and (b) σ_λ has Zariski-dense image for a density-one set of λ. Then Theorem 3.1 applied to the reductions of σ determines the square class of L(X, σ) in E(√q)^×/2 up to multiplication by 2.
contract.note: Not used elsewhere in the paper.

contract.name: The defect δ(X, ρ) and Frobenius of k
contract.statement: δ(X, ρ) := L^*(X, ρ)/c_et(X, ρ) ∈ ℓ^×/2 (similarly for GSp-admissible ρ^{(g)}). For M/Q finite Galois unramified at p, Frob_k ∈ Gal(M/Q) is the conjugacy class of Frob(ϖ/p)^n for q = p^n.

contract.name: Step A: the defect is a Dirichlet character
contract.statement: For fixed r and ℓ there is a quadratic character χ_{r,ℓ} : Gal(Q̄/Q) → {±1}, unramified outside the primes dividing #Sp_{2r}(ℓ), such that δ(X, ρ) = χ_{r,ℓ}(Frob_k) (under {±1} ≅ ℓ^×/2) for every GSp-admissible (X, ρ) over k.
contract.note: The proof uses Lemma 5.1.1, which fails for r = 1, #ℓ = 9 (sourceIssues E4).

contract.name: Step B: χ_{r,ℓ} is unramified outside 2ℓ
contract.statement: For #ℓ ≡ ±1 (mod 8), the character χ_{r,ℓ} of Step A is unramified outside 2ℓ: for each odd prime m ≠ ℓ there is a Galois extension M* of Q unramified at m such that for every sufficiently large prime p split in M* there is a GSp-admissible (X, ρ) over F_{p^j}, j odd, with δ(X, ρ) = 1.

contract.name: Steps A and B imply Theorem 3.1
contract.statement: If χ_{r,ℓ} is unramified outside 2ℓ then χ_{r,ℓ}(Frob_p) = (Z/p) with Z ∈ ⟨−1, 2, ℓ_0⟩; writing Z = Z_0 or Z_0ℓ_0′ (ℓ_0′ = (−1)^{(ℓ_0−1)/2}ℓ_0) and using (ℓ_0′/p)^n = (q/ℓ_0) = 1 for admissible (X, ρ), δ(X, ρ) = (Z_0/p)^n, a character mod 8 of q = p^n, which is 1 when q ≡ 1 (mod 8).

contract.name: Hurwitz stacks 𝔐^G_g and 𝔐^{G*}_g
contract.statement: For G = Sp_{2r}(ℓ), N = #G: the Deligne–Mumford stack 𝔐^G_g over Z[1/N] of smooth projective genus-g curves Σ/S with a finite étale G-torsor f : Σ̃ → Σ whose geometric fibres Σ̃_s are irreducible; and its twisted form 𝔐^{G*}_g for G̃ = GSp_{2r}(ℓ) with an identification of the associated ℓ^×-cover with the cyclotomic one (fibres with #ℓ − 1 components). Over C a component is 𝒯/Γ̃_0 for Teichmüller space 𝒯 and the central extension Γ̃_0 of the stabilizer Γ_0 of a surjection π_1(Σ) → G by Z(G); 𝔐^G_g is a gerbe over Deligne–Mumford's stack of Teichmüller level structures. Admissible pairs give k-points of 𝔐^G_g, GSp-admissible pairs k-points of 𝔐^{G*}_g.

contract.name: Livingston–Dunfield–Thurston: mapping class group orbits on surjections
contract.statement: For a finite group G with H_2(G, Z) = 0 and g sufficiently large, the mapping class group of a closed genus-g surface Σ acts transitively on the set of conjugacy classes of surjections π_1(Σ) → G (Dunfield–Thurston, Thm. 6.25, after Livingston). In general the orbits are classified by the image of [Σ] in H_2(G, Z).
contract.note: The paper notes that Dunfield–Thurston's Theorem 6.25 is slightly misstated (the action is by the mapping class group modulo the group).

contract.name: Lemma 5.1.1: irreducibility in large genus
contract.statement: If H_2(Sp_{2r}(ℓ), Z) = 0, i.e. unless r = 1 and #ℓ = 9, there is g_0(r, ℓ) such that for g ≥ g_0 the Q̄-fibre of 𝔐^G_g is irreducible (and so is that of 𝔐^{G*}_g).
contract.note: Stated as corrected; the paper asserts it for all (r, ℓ) (sourceIssues E4).

contract.name: The universal classes 𝔜 and 𝔜′
contract.statement: On the universal curve π : 𝔘* → 𝔐^{G*} with its G̃-cover 𝔘* → BG̃: 𝔜 ∈ H^1_et(𝔐^{G*}, Z/2) is π_*(pullback of c_et) (trace shifting degree by 2), and 𝔜′ ∈ H^1(𝔐^{G*}, ℓ^×/2) classifies the spinor-norm torsor of the orthogonal local system 𝒪 = R^1π_*𝒮 (𝒮 the symplectic ℓ-local system, with pairing to ℓ(1)). For a GSp-admissible (X, ρ) over k, 𝔜 and 𝔜′ specialize to c_et(X, ρ) and L(X, ρ) in H^1(k, Z/2) = k^×/2.
contract.note: Uses étale cohomology of Artin stacks (Laszlo–Olsson).

contract.name: Lemma 5.2.1: 𝔜 = 𝔜′ on the geometric generic fibre
contract.statement: 𝔜 and 𝔜′ coincide on 𝔐^{G*}_{Q̄}.
contract.note: For a loop γ, 𝔜(γ) = trace_M(ρ^*c_et) on the mapping torus M and 𝔜′(γ) = spinor norm of the monodromy on H^1(fibre, ρ), equal by (1.5); here the coefficients are finite, where the paper proves (1.5) only in characteristic 0 (sourceIssues E25). The stack is handled through a smooth cover (Y × E)/Δ with E an approximation of BΔ (Totaro).

contract.name: Lemma 5.3.1: 𝔜 − 𝔜′ comes from Z[1/N]
contract.statement: For g ≥ g_0(r, ℓ), 𝔜 − 𝔜′ is the pullback to 𝔐^{G*} of a class in H^1(Z[1/N], Z/2), i.e. of a quadratic character unramified outside N.
contract.note: Uses irreducibility (Lemma 5.1.1), purity (injectivity of H^1(𝔐^{G*}) → H^1(𝔐^{G*}_Q)) and W-points of 𝔐^{G*} for each w ∤ N (Sp_{2r}(ℓ) is 2-generated).

contract.name: §5.4 Claim: odd-degree cyclic covers preserve δ
contract.statement: Let (X, ρ) be GSp-admissible, m odd and prime to ℓ with ℓ of odd order t modulo m, and f : X̃ → X a Z/m-Galois cover by a geometrically irreducible smooth proper curve. Then (X̃, f^*ρ) is GSp-admissible and δ(X, ρ) = δ(X̃, f^*ρ).
contract.note: c_et is preserved since f^* : H^3(X, Z/2) → H^3(X̃, Z/2) is an isomorphism; for L^* the Artin decomposition over the characters of Z/m, the functional equation and §5.4.1 show the extra factors are squares.

contract.name: §5.4.1: ε-factors of twists of symplectic systems
contract.statement: For ρ symplectic and unramified with det ρ = 1 and χ a character, ε(ρ ⊗ χ) = ε(χ)^{dim ρ} (an equality, not only of square classes); in particular ε(ρ ⊗ χ) is a square.

contract.name: §5.5 Claim: raising the genus
contract.statement: For each GSp-admissible (X, ρ) over k there is g_0′(X, ρ) such that for every g ≥ g_0′ there is a GSp-admissible (X′, ρ′) of genus g over k with δ(X′, ρ′) = δ(X, ρ).
contract.note: X′ is a ramified Z/M-cover, M a product of primes m ≡ 3 (mod 4) with q and ℓ of odd order mod m and gcd of the (m−1)/2 equal to 1, built by class field theory and Riemann–Hurwitz.

contract.name: §6.1 Claim: totally real fields with prescribed unit reduction
contract.statement: For a finite field ℓ with #ℓ ≡ ±1 (mod 8) and an odd prime m ≠ char ℓ, there is a totally real field F with (i) [F:Q] ≥ 3, (ii) D_F prime to m, (iii) a prime λ_0 with o_F/λ_0 ≅ ℓ such that U_F^+ (totally positive classes in H^1(o_F[1/2], Z/2) ⊂ F^×/2) maps trivially to ℓ^×/2, and (iv) a Galois extension M ⊃ F of Q unramified at m such that for every p unramified, prime to 2ℓ and completely split in M, U_F^{(p+)} also maps trivially to ℓ^×/2.
contract.note: F = Q[x]/f for f = x^n + Σa_i x^{n−i} ± ℓ with real roots, roots ≡ 1 (mod 8) in Q_2, a prescribed ℓ_0-adic factorization, discriminant prime to m and irreducible; λ_0 = (α) with α a square at the places above 2.

contract.name: Compatible systems on the Hilbert–Siegel variety
contract.statement: For each place λ of F with residue characteristic prime to Δ, 𝒮[1/λ] carries the étale local system ρ_λ of o_{F,λ}-modules from the Tate module of the universal abelian scheme, pure of weight −1, coming over C from a local system of o_F-modules; at an F_q-point (q prime to Δ) the trace of Frobenius on ρ_λ lies in F and is independent of λ (Shimura, 11.10). The geometric image of ρ_λ is Sp_{2r}(o_{F,λ}) for λ ∤ e, and Zariski dense for λ | e.

contract.name: Vanishing of H^1 of the Hilbert–Siegel variety
contract.statement: H^1(S_C, ρ_λ) = 0; equivalently H^1(Γ, F^{2r} ⊗_ι C) = 0 for an arithmetic Γ ≤ Sp_{2r}(F) and each embedding ι : F → C.
contract.note: The paper sketches this from superrigidity or the congruence subgroup property ([F:Q] ≥ 3 gives real rank ≥ 3).

contract.name: Lemma 6.3.1: α_C = 0
contract.statement: Let α ∈ H^3_et(𝒮, ℓ^×/2) be the pullback of c_et along the reduction of ρ_{λ_0} (a GSp_{2r}(ℓ)-local system). Its restriction to S_C is trivial.
contract.note: Over C the local system lifts to Sp_{2r}(o_F); c_et then factors through U_F, landing in U_F^+ by the vanishing of c_31 on Sp_{2r}(R), and U_F^+ → ℓ^×/2 is trivial by §6.1 (iii).

contract.name: Lemma 6.3.2: killing α on special fibres
contract.statement: There is a finite Galois extension M/Q, unramified outside 2Δ (so at m), such that Frob_k trivial in Gal(M/Q) implies α_k = 0.
contract.note: Rπ_*(Z/2) on Z[1/Δ] has lcc cohomology sheaves (via the normal crossings compactification, SGA 4½ 'Théorèmes de finitude', appendix); M is the maximal exponent-2 abelian extension, unramified outside 2Δ, of the splitting field of H^2(S_Q̄, Z/2).

contract.name: Slicing down to a surface
contract.statement: For a geometrically irreducible component S° ⊂ P^m_{M_0} (M_0 = Q(ζ_e)) of dimension ≥ 3 whose boundary in its closure has codimension ≥ 3, a general M_0-rational hyperplane section is smooth, geometrically irreducible, has boundary codimension ≥ 3, and induces an isomorphism on π_1 of the complex points (Goresky–MacPherson, Stratified Morse Theory II.1.1), hence on H^1(−, ρ_λ). Iterating, one reaches a smooth projective surface with the same properties (a)–(d) of §6.4, which spread out over o_{M_0}[1/S] and specialize to F_p for large p split in M_0 (geometric monodromy preserved by SGA 1 X; H^1 = 0 by proper smooth base change).

contract.name: Guralnick–Tiep: the eighth-moment criterion for SO
contract.statement: For a reductive algebraic subgroup Γ ⊂ O(W), W orthogonal over a field of characteristic zero (of large enough dimension), dim(W^{⊗8})^Γ = dim(W^{⊗8})^{SO(W)} = C_4 = 8!/(4!·2^4) implies Γ ⊃ SO(W) (Guralnick–Tiep, Thm. 1.4).

contract.name: Lemma 6.4.2: points impose independent conditions on hypersurfaces
contract.statement: For pairwise distinct x_1, …, x_r in S°(F_q) and D ≥ r − 1, vanishing at all x_i is a codimension-r condition on Γ(S°_{F_q}, 𝒪(D)) (Poonen, Lemma 2.1), so the fraction of degree-D slices through them is (q^{E−r} − 1)/(q^E − 1) = q^{−r}(1 + O(q^{r−E})), E = dim Γ(S°, 𝒪(D)).
contract.note: Stated as corrected: the paper's choice of D does not guarantee D ≥ r − 1 (sourceIssues E8).

contract.name: Lemma 6.4.1: slices with nonvanishing central value
contract.statement: There are D_0 and p_0(D) such that for D ≥ D_0 and p ≥ p_0(D) split in M_0, the orthogonal local system 𝖶 (fibre H^1(X_h, ρ_λ)(−1)) on the space ℋ_D of smooth degree-D slices of the surface S°_{F_p} has geometric monodromy Zariski dense in SO; and there are an odd j and h ∈ ℋ_D(F_{p^j}) with slice X = X_h a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve such that (i) L(X, ρ_λ, 1) ≠ 0, (ii) the geometric monodromy of (X, ρ_λ) equals that of (S°, ρ_λ), (iii) j is odd.
contract.note: Method of moments: the eighth moment of the Frobenius traces on H^1(X_h, ρ_λ) over ℋ_D is bounded by C_4 q^4(1 + o(1)) using Lemma 6.4.2, Deligne's bound (6.15) and a Möbius inversion over set partitions; then Guralnick–Tiep and Chebotarev. (ii) is Grothendieck's Lefschetz theorem (SGA 2 XII Cor. 3.5).

contract.name: Lemma 6.5.1: c_et of the slices
contract.statement: There is a Galois extension M_1/Q, unramified at m, such that for the slices (X, ρ) of Lemma 6.4.1 (ρ the reduction of ρ_{λ_0}), c_et(X, ρ) is trivial whenever p is split in M_1.
contract.note: The printed statement says 'unramified outside m' (sourceIssues E11).

contract.name: Lemma 6.5.2: L-value of the slices
contract.statement: There is a Galois extension M_2/Q, unramified at m, such that L(X, ρ) is trivial whenever p is split in M_2 and sufficiently large: L(X, ρ_·, 1) ∈ F^× is totally positive (Riemann hypothesis) with even valuation at every λ ∤ 2p (Lemma 3.9.1), so its class lies in U_F^{(p+)}, which maps trivially to ℓ^×/2 by §6.1 (iv).

contract.name: c_et on the quaternion group
contract.statement: The pullback of the étale Chern class from H^3(SL_2(Q(i)), Q(i)^×/2) to Q_8 (Pauli matrices) is the unique nonzero class of H^3(Q_8, Z/2), valued in the subgroup generated by i: for q ≡ 5 (mod 8), Q_8 is a 2-Sylow subgroup of SL_2(F_q) and H_3(Q_8) → H_3(SL_2(F_q)) is onto, while i is a nonsquare in F_q.

contract.name: Both sides of Theorem 3.1 for quaternionic covers of curves
contract.statement: A Q_8-cover of a curve X/F_q is a quadratic étale X̃/X with involution σ and α : Pic(X̃) → Z/4 with σ^*α = −α and α|_{Pic X} the character of X̃/X (D.1). Then ∫_X of the generator of H^3(Q_8) equals y(ℒ_x), y ∈ H^1(X, Z/2) evaluated by class field theory on the 2-torsion bundle of x (Lemma D.4.1: ∫x² ∪ y = ∫β′(x) ∪ y, (D.2)); and L(X, ρ, 1/√q) = L(X̃, α, 1/√q) = Σ_k q^{−k/2}L_k with L_k = Σ_{deg D=k} α(D), symmetric under k ↔ 2g − 2 − k with sign α(𝒦). For genus-2 X : y² = xQ(x) with X̃ : w² = Q(t²) this gives qL(½, ρ) = 2q + Σ_{deg D=2} α(D) (D.6), and the invariant (D.5) vanishes iff (0) − (∞) ∈ π_*(ker α²).
contract.note: Several slips in D.2–D.6 are recorded as sourceIssues E22–E24.

contract.name: Numerical examples beyond the hypotheses of Theorem 3.1
contract.statement: Each of the hyperelliptic curves 2x⁸ + 2x⁶z² − 4x⁴z⁴ − 3x²z⁶ − 3z⁸ + y² = 0 over F_5, x⁸ + 4x⁶z² + 2x⁴z⁴ + 3x²z⁶ + 5z⁸ + y² = 0 over F_11, 5x⁸ + 2x⁶z² − 6x⁴z⁴ − 7x²z⁶ + 7z⁸ + y² = 0 over F_13 and 5x⁸ + 15x⁶z² + 15x⁴z⁴ + 2x²z⁶ + 12z⁸ + y² = 0 over F_17 carries a quaternionic local system with nonsquare qL(½) and nonvanishing invariant (D.5); in all computed examples 'qL(½) is a square' coincided with vanishing of (D.5).
contract.note: Recomputed independently (class groups and all 8 admissible α per curve): every nonzero qL(½) is ~ i and the pairing is nonzero; on the F_5 curve 4 of the 8 α have L(½) = 0, a case the paper does not discuss.
